subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For ordinary Claude CLI sessions that are already over the native context cap, should OpenClaw rely on Claude Code native compaction, fail loudly with recovery guidance, or add an OpenClaw-owned fallback/import compaction path?
rationale: Current source intentionally defers ordinary claude-cli compaction to the backend, while the reported user harm is an OpenClaw Dashboard recovery contract; automation cannot choose that ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery
options.body: Keep provider-owned native compaction, but detect unusable over-cap/no-summary states and preserve the existing session while showing clear export, manual-prune, or new-session recovery guidance.

options.title: Trust Claude Native Ownership
options.body: Keep the current no-op deferral and treat over-cap recovery as Claude Code-owned, with docs/diagnostics clarifying that OpenClaw cannot compact those native transcripts.

options.title: Add OpenClaw Fallback Compaction
options.body: Implement a bounded Claude transcript import or fallback summarizer path for over-cap native sessions, accepting the larger compatibility and transcript-ownership surface.

recommendation.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep provider-owned native compaction, but detect unusable over-cap/no-summary states and preserve the existing session while showing clear export, manual-prune, or new-session recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current native compaction ownership contract and are the best match in the available history for deciding whether that contract should change.
